claims.explanation: Fluspirilene is a diphenylbutylpiperidine that blocks voltage-gated calcium channels and dopamine receptors, and its anticancer activity has been linked to CDK2 inhibition and autophagy induction. Sensitivity may be enhanced in cells with intact p53 signaling and high calcium-channel dependence, while PTEN loss and RAS/BRAF activation could provide survival signals that reduce killing.

features.basis: Most sensitive lines carry TP53 mutations, but many resistant lines also do; weak pattern
PTEN-mutant lines appear enriched among resistant lines, possibly via PI3K/AKT survival signaling
BRAF-mutant melanomas and colorectal lines are present in resistant set, suggesting MAPK-driven survival
KRAS-mutant lines appear in both sets but several resistant lines carry KRAS mutations
Fluspirilene blocks L-type calcium channels; high expression may increase dependence
Fluspirilene inhibits N-type calcium channels; expression may predict sensitivity
Fluspirilene is a dopamine receptor antagonist; DRD2 expression may mediate antiproliferative effects
Fluspirilene identified as CDK2 inhibitor; high CDK2 activity may predict response
Fluspirilene induces autophagy via calpain1-mediated ATG5 cleavage; full-length ATG5 levels may affect response
Calpain1 cleaves ATG5; high calpain1 may reduce autophagy induction by fluspirilene
Fluspirilene suppresses STAT3; high STAT3 signaling may reduce sensitivity
EGFR-mutant lung lines appear in sensitive set, but also in resistant set; weak evidence
